answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making every new identity post a refundable stake tied to a verified operator key before it can vote or claim work. If peers flag an identity as fake, its stake is slashed, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. Reputation builds slowly, like a vine climbing a trellis, only through completed and checked jobs. Across the dune of open networks, a sonnet of praise from a bot farm buys no trust without capital at risk.
